title.narrative: Lifesaving and resilience-building WASH & FSL intervention in Dar'a and DZ - EH

description.narrative: Oxfam proposes a 12 -month multisectoral humanitarian response in underserved communities of Izra' and Da'el sub -districts in Dar'a governorate and Deir ez -Zor city in Deir ez -Zor governorate. The project aims to improve access to safe water, sanitation, food, and essential services for 75,280 vulnerable individuals, including returnees, IDPs, and host communities, in alignment with the clusters' objectives priorities. These areas are among the SHF -prioritized sub -districts with inter -sector severity scores of 4 and are experiencing increased pressure on services due to recent returns and ongoing displacement. Additionally, Oxfam coordinated with relevant sectors, local authorities, and humanitarian actors (including EPDC, TGH, PUI and GVC) to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication The proposed intervention is informed by Oxfam's assessments and consultations with local authorities, community representatives, and sectors. In Dar'a, Oxfam will rehabilitate three boreholes (two in Mahjeh and one in Abtaa) with solar systems, and upgrade water networks in Izra' city to improve water access for 18,500 people. In parallel, Oxfam will address sanitation risks for 20,000 individuals by repairing sewage systems in Izra' and Dael, mitigating environmental and public health hazards. Additionally, the project will rehabilitate a bakery in Izra' town, adding a second production line to increase daily bread output from 8.3 to over 16 tons. This will directly benefit 33,880 people by improving access to affordable bread and reducing food insecurity. The bakery design includes gender -sensitive considerations such as separate queues, as well as considering PWD and elderly -friendly access. In Deir ez -Zor, Oxfam will scale up its MPCA response, through six rounds of Multi -Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), 580 households (2,900 individuals) will receive timely support to meet urgent needs, including food, rent, and essential services. This builds on Oxfam's ongoing MPCA programming
